Use `granularity: "range"` with `end_line` only when the full finding genuinely spans multiple changed right-side lines. Prefer a single changed line.

+package interactive
+
+import "sync/atomic"
+
+// gitHookContext records that this process was invoked as a git hook. It is a
+// one-way latch set once during command setup, so reads are cheap and cannot
+// race with a later change.
+var gitHookContext atomic.Bool
+
+// MarkGitHookContext declares that this process is running as a git hook, which
+// changes what a controlling terminal implies: git was run by something else —
+// possibly a TUI client that gave us a private terminal it only reads from — so
+// a terminal we can open is not necessarily one a user can answer on. See
+// jobcontrol_unix.go for the check this enables and why it is scoped here rather
+// than applied to every `entire` invocation.
+//
+// Called from the `entire hooks git` command tree, which every git hook funnels
+// through. Direct CLI invocations never set it and keep the plain terminal
+// detection.
+func MarkGitHookContext() { gitHookContext.Store(true) }
+
+// inGitHookContext reports whether MarkGitHookContext was called.
+func inGitHookContext() bool { return gitHookContext.Load() }

diff --git a/cmd/entire/cli/interactive/jobcontrol_unix.go b/cmd/entire/cli/interactive/jobcontrol_unix.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..5563cdd0
--- /dev/null
+++ b/cmd/entire/cli/interactive/jobcontrol_unix.go
@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+//go:build darwin || linux
+
+package interactive
+
+import "golang.org/x/sys/unix"
+
+// ttyIsPrivateSession reports whether our controlling terminal was created for
+// this command alone, rather than handed to us by a user's interactive shell.
+//
+// Output-capturing git clients don't merely inherit the user's terminal: lazygit
+// runs `git commit` on a *fresh pty*, and making a pty into a controlling
+// terminal requires setsid + TIOCSCTTY. The git process therefore becomes a
+// session leader on a private terminal — one that opens cleanly and sits in
+// canonical mode, so neither the /dev/tty probe nor the raw-mode check
+// (rawmode_unix.go) can tell that nobody is reading it. lazygit only renders
+// that pty's output; it does not forward keystrokes to it, so a prompt there
+// never receives an answer: the commit blocks and the UI appears frozen.
+//
+// Job control is the discriminator. An interactive shell puts every foreground
+// command in its own process group, distinct from the session leader's own, so a
+// human's `git commit` always runs with pgrp != sid. A command handed a private
+// session is both session and process-group leader, so every process in it (git,
+// the hook script, us) sees pgrp == sid.
+//
+// Measured on Linux against lazygit 0.48 (sid == pgrp == the git pid, on a
+// second pty distinct from lazygit's own) and against interactive bash and
+// busybox sh (sid = the shell, pgrp = the git job). This shape follows from the
+// setsid a private controlling terminal requires, so unlike the pty's window
+// size — which lazygit presets to 80x24 in current master — it does not drift
+// with a client's rendering details.
+//
+// The known trade-off is `ssh -t host git commit` and `script -c`, which also
+// setsid onto a fresh pty but do forward input: those lose the prompt and fall
+// back to the non-interactive path (for commit linking, that means auto-link —
+// the prompt's own default).
+func ttyIsPrivateSession() bool {
+	sid, err := unix.Getsid(0)
+	if err != nil {
+		// Can't tell — fail open. This check may only ever suppress prompts we
+		// positively know are unusable.
+		return false
+	}
+	return sid == unix.Getpgrp()
+}
diff --git a/cmd/entire/cli/interactive/jobcontrol_unix_test.go b/cmd/entire/cli/interactive/jobcontrol_unix_test.go
new file mode 100644
index 00000000..25d78816
--- /dev/null
+++ b/cmd/entire/cli/interactive/jobcontrol_unix_test.go
@@ -0,0 +1,72 @@
+//go:build darwin || linux
+
+package interactive
+
+import (
+	"os"
+	"os/exec"
+	"strings"
+	"syscall"
+	"testing"
+)
+
+// envJobControlHelper makes the test binary re-exec itself as a helper that
+// reports ttyIsPrivateSession() from a process whose session/process-group shape
+// this test controls. The shapes are what matters, and a test can only set them
+// on a child, not on itself.
+const envJobControlHelper = "ENTIRE_TEST_JOBCONTROL_HELPER"
+
+// TestMain serves the helper mode described above before handing off to the
+// normal test run.
+func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
+	if os.Getenv(envJobControlHelper) != "" {
+		if ttyIsPrivateSession() {
+			os.Stdout.WriteString("true\n")
+		} else {
+			os.Stdout.WriteString("false\n")
+		}
+		os.Exit(0)
+	}
+	os.Exit(m.Run())
+}
+
+// runHelper re-execs the test binary with attr applied and returns what
+// ttyIsPrivateSession() reported there.
+func runHelper(t *testing.T, attr *syscall.SysProcAttr) string {
+	t.Helper()
+
+	self, err := os.Executable()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("os.Executable: %v", err)
+	}
+	cmd := exec.CommandContext(t.Context(), self)
+	cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), envJobControlHelper+"=1")
+	cmd.SysProcAttr = attr
+	out, err := cmd.Output()
+	if err != nil {
+		t.Fatalf("helper: %v (output %q)", err, out)
+	}
+	return strings.TrimSpace(string(out))
+}
+
+// A process given its own session (what setsid + a fresh pty does, and what
+// lazygit's output-capturing `git commit` runs inside) is both session and
+// process-group leader, so it must report a private session.
+func TestTTYIsPrivateSession_OwnSessionIsPrivate(t *testing.T) {
+	t.Parallel()
+
+	if got := runHelper(t, &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setsid: true}); got != "true" {

+//go:build darwin || linux
+
+package interactive
+
+import "golang.org/x/sys/unix"
+
+// ttyIsPrivateSession reports whether our controlling terminal was created for
+// this command alone, rather than handed to us by a user's interactive shell.
+//
+// Output-capturing git clients don't merely inherit the user's terminal: lazygit
+// runs `git commit` on a *fresh pty*, and making a pty into a controlling
+// terminal requires setsid + TIOCSCTTY. The git process therefore becomes a
+// session leader on a private terminal — one that opens cleanly and sits in
+// canonical mode, so neither the /dev/tty probe nor the raw-mode check
+// (rawmode_unix.go) can tell that nobody is reading it. lazygit only renders
+// that pty's output; it does not forward keystrokes to it, so a prompt there
+// never receives an answer: the commit blocks and the UI appears frozen.
+//
+// Job control is the discriminator. An interactive shell puts every foreground
+// command in its own process group, distinct from the session leader's own, so a
+// human's `git commit` always runs with pgrp != sid. A command handed a private
+// session is both session and process-group leader, so every process in it (git,
+// the hook script, us) sees pgrp == sid.
+//
+// Measured on Linux against lazygit 0.48 (sid == pgrp == the git pid, on a
+// second pty distinct from lazygit's own) and against interactive bash and
+// busybox sh (sid = the shell, pgrp = the git job). This shape follows from the
+// setsid a private controlling terminal requires, so unlike the pty's window
+// size — which lazygit presets to 80x24 in current master — it does not drift
+// with a client's rendering details.
+//
+// The known trade-off is `ssh -t host git commit` and `script -c`, which also
+// setsid onto a fresh pty but do forward input: those lose the prompt and fall
+// back to the non-interactive path (for commit linking, that means auto-link —
+// the prompt's own default).
+func ttyIsPrivateSession() bool {
+	sid, err := unix.Getsid(0)
+	if err != nil {
+		// Can't tell — fail open. This check may only ever suppress prompts we
+		// positively know are unusable.
+		return false
+	}
+	return sid == unix.Getpgrp()
+}

1	// Package interactive provides TTY-related helpers shared between the cli
2	// and strategy packages without inducing an import cycle (strategy cannot
3	// import cli).
4	package interactive
5	
6	import (
7		"io"
8		"os"
9		"testing"
10	
11		"golang.org/x/term"
12	)
13	
14	// EnvTestTTY is the env-var name for the force-interactive test override.
15	//   - EnvTestTTY=1 → CanPromptInteractively returns true.
16	//   - EnvTestTTY set to any other value → returns false.
17	//   - EnvTestTTY unset → real detection via testing.Testing(), agent
18	//     sentinels, CI, then /dev/tty probe.
19	const EnvTestTTY = "ENTIRE_TEST_TTY"
20	
21	// CanPromptInteractively reports whether interactive confirmation prompts
22	// (huh forms, yes/no questions, etc.) can be shown. Returns false in CI,
23	// agent subprocesses that inherit a TTY but can't respond to prompts,
24	// and other environments without a controlling TTY.
25	//
26	// Precedence (first match wins):
27	//  1. EnvTestTTY=1 forces interactive ON; any other non-empty value forces OFF.
28	//  2. testing.Testing() — `go test` runs default to OFF so in-process tests
29	//     don't hang on developer terminals that happen to have a real /dev/tty.
30	//     Subprocess tests must spawn via execx.NonInteractive (or set EnvTestTTY).
31	//  3. Agent sentinels — vendor-set by agent subprocesses.
32	//  4. CI=<non-empty-non-false> — de-facto CI convention.
33	//  5. Git-hook context with a private session — when we run as a git hook (see
34	//     MarkGitHookContext) and our terminal session was created for this command
35	//     alone, git was run by a client capturing our output: lazygit gives `git
36	//     commit` its own pty and only renders what comes back, so a prompt there is
37	//     never answered and the commit hangs. See jobcontrol_unix.go.
38	//  6. /dev/tty probe, plus its terminal mode: a controlling terminal held in raw
39	//     mode belongs to a full-screen TUI (gitui, tig, …) that spawned us, not to
40	//     a shell we can prompt. See rawmode_unix.go.
41	func CanPromptInteractively() bool {
42		if v := os.Getenv(EnvTestTTY); v != "" {
43			return v == "1"
44		}
45		if testing.Testing() {
46			return false
47		}
48		if isAgentSubprocessEnv() {
49			return false
50		}
51		// CI=<non-empty> is the de-facto CI-provider convention (GitHub Actions,
52		// CircleCI, GitLab, Travis, Buildkite). Self-hosted runners expose /dev/tty,
53		// so the probe below isn't enough — an interactive prompt on CI hangs.
54		// CI=false is the `is-ci` escape hatch for developers who need to override
55		// an inherited value.
56		if v := os.Getenv("CI"); v != "" && v != "false" {
57			return false
58		}
59	
60		// A git hook inherits whatever terminal the client that ran git left it, and
61		// a TUI client hands us a private one it only reads from. This is scoped to
62		// hook context because one-shot interactive invocations (`ssh -t host entire
63		// enable`, `docker run -it … entire enable`) have the same private-session
64		// shape but do forward the user's keystrokes.
65		if inGitHookContext() && ttyIsPrivateSession() {
66			return false
67		}
68	
69		tty, err := os.OpenFile("/dev/tty", os.O_RDWR, 0)
70		if err != nil {
71			return false
72		}
73		defer tty.Close()
74		// Having a controlling terminal isn't enough — a TUI that spawned us holds
75		// that same terminal in raw mode for its own screen and keys. See
76		// rawmode_unix.go.
77		return !ttyInRawMode(tty)
78	}
79	
80	// UnderTest reports whether the process is running in a test context — either
81	// inside `go test` (testing.Testing()) or with EnvTestTTY explicitly set. Use
82	// to skip operations that read from the real terminal (e.g. opening /dev/tty)
83	// even when CanPromptInteractively() returns true.
84	func UnderTest() bool {
85		return testing.Testing() || os.Getenv(EnvTestTTY) != ""
86	}
87	
88	// isAgentSubprocessEnv reports whether the env indicates we're running inside
89	// an agent subprocess that inherited a TTY but can't respond to prompts:
90	//   - GEMINI_CLI=1: Gemini CLI shell tool (https://geminicli.com/docs/tools/shell/)
91	//   - COPILOT_CLI=1: Copilot CLI hook subprocesses (v0.0.421+)
92	//   - PI_CODING_AGENT=true: Pi Coding Agent shell tool
93	//   - GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0: caller (CI, Factory AI Droid, etc.) asked git
94	//     to stop prompting; respect it from git-hook context too.
95	func isAgentSubprocessEnv() bool {
96		return os.Getenv("GEMINI_CLI") != "" ||
97			os.Getenv("COPILOT_CLI") != "" ||
98			os.Getenv("PI_CODING_AGENT") != "" ||
99			os.Getenv("GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT") == "0"
100	}
101	
102	// IsTerminalReader reports whether r is an *os.File backed by a terminal.
103	// It is useful when an explicitly interactive command needs to distinguish a
104	// human at stdin from an agent process that merely inherited a controlling TTY.
105	func IsTerminalReader(r io.Reader) bool {
106		f, ok := r.(*os.File)
107		if !ok {
108			return false
109		}
110		return term.IsTerminal(int(f.Fd())) //nolint:gosec // G115: uintptr->int is safe for fd
111	}
112	
113	// IsTerminalWriter reports whether w is an *os.File backed by a terminal.
114	// Use for deciding on color, pager, progress bars, or other writer-scoped
115	// TTY formatting. For "can I prompt the user?" use CanPromptInteractively.
116	func IsTerminalWriter(w io.Writer) bool {
117		f, ok := w.(*os.File)
118		if !ok {
119			return false
120		}
121		return term.IsTerminal(int(f.Fd())) //nolint:gosec // G115: uintptr->int is safe for fd
122	}
123	
124	// ShouldStyle reports whether ANSI-styled output (color, bold, rendered
125	// markdown) should be written to w. It is the single gate for writer-scoped
126	// styling decisions: NO_COLOR disables styling per https://no-color.org,
127	// legacy consoles that can't handle ANSI escapes are excluded, and otherwise
128	// the answer is whether w is a terminal.
129	func ShouldStyle(w io.Writer) bool {
130		return shouldStyle(os.Getenv("NO_COLOR"), os.Getenv("TERM"), IsTerminalWriter(w))
131	}
132	
133	// shouldStyle is the pure decision behind ShouldStyle, split out so tests can
134	// exercise the NO_COLOR/TERM gates with a simulated terminal writer — `go
135	// test` never has a real one, so testing through ShouldStyle would
136	// short-circuit on the terminal check and never reach the earlier gates.
137	func shouldStyle(noColor, term string, isTerminalWriter bool) bool {
138		if noColor != "" {
139			return false
140		}
141		if termLacksANSI(term) {
142			return false
143		}
144		return isTerminalWriter
145	}
146	
147	// termLacksANSI reports whether term identifies a legacy console that does
148	// not reliably handle ANSI escape sequences. The canonical case is
149	// TERM=cygwin: writing the ESC byte (0x1B) ends up rendered as the CP437
150	// glyph U+2190 LEFTWARDS ARROW ("←") instead of starting an SGR sequence, so
151	// styled output appears as literal text like "←[32m●←[m" (see GH #1267).
152	func termLacksANSI(term string) bool {
153		return term == "cygwin"
154	}
